gaps.sentence: We were asked to ___ an experiment in the laboratory.
gaps.explanation: do an experiment is the standard collocation in scientific contexts.

gaps.sentence: Can we ___ a phone call before we leave?
gaps.explanation: make a phone call / make a call is the standard collocation.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: My brother and I ___ turns washing up after dinner.
gaps.explanation: take turns means to do something one after another, alternating.

gaps.sentence: The doctor has ___ detailed records of every patient since 1990.
gaps.explanation: keep records (of something) is the fixed collocation for storing information.

gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.
